rules.instruction: When the description says an event sets back an ongoing activity and that activity must then carry on afterwards: Model the setback handling as its own step after the event. Then add a task that resumes the same ongoing activity after the handling, and connect it back into that activity's flow so the process returns to the activity. Do not let the flow end at the setback.
rules.situation: the description says an event sets back an ongoing activity and that activity must then carry on afterwards

rules.instruction: When the description states an action in a sentence whose main verb names that action, and the label a generator would give the corresponding task replaces that verb with a different verb or adds an object or qualifier the sentence does not contain: Label the task with the verb and object the description uses for that action, keeping the description's own verb (for example, the verb of a sentence that states a state change or a start). Do not substitute a new verb-object phrase that describes a different or more specific action, and do not add qualifiers such as 'urgency' or 'to farm' that the sentence does not state.
rules.situation: the description states an action in a sentence whose main verb names that action, and the label a generator would give the corresponding task replaces that verb with a different verb or adds an object or qualifier the sentence does not contain

rules.instruction: When the description names a human actor and an automated agent that each perform activities within the same system, and the description attributes activities to each of them: Model one bpmn:participant pool that represents the system as a whole. Inside it, create one bpmn:lane for each actor, named after that actor, and assign every flow node to the lane of the actor who performs it. Keep all sequence flows within the single owning process, and use message flows only if the actors exchange messages across separate participant pools.
rules.situation: the description names a human actor and an automated agent that each perform activities within the same system, and the description attributes activities to each of them

rules.instruction: When the description states that some items are required to create tools, and those tools are needed to gather other items (a dependency between items): Model the creation of those tools as its own task, named after the description's wording, and place it in the flow before the gathering task that depends on it, so the dependency is visible as a sequence. Do not drop the tool-creation step or fold it into the gathering task.
rules.situation: the description states that some items are required to create tools, and those tools are needed to gather other items (a dependency between items)

rules.instruction: When the description states that an activity can be performed at any time while a longer ongoing activity runs, with no condition or message that starts it, and the activity is not part of the main sequence of that ongoing activity: Model that activity as a task inside the scope of the ongoing activity, not as a step in its main sequence and not dropped. Place it on a branch that runs alongside the ongoing activity, starting when the ongoing activity starts and ending when it ends, so it can be performed repeatedly or not at all during that period. Do not connect it with a sequence flow that makes it wait for the ongoing activity to finish, and do not omit it.
rules.situation: the description states that an activity can be performed at any time while a longer ongoing activity runs, with no condition or message that starts it, and the activity is not part of the main sequence of that ongoing activity

rules.instruction: When the description states that after an automated process has finished, a participant may perform one or more optional follow-up actions (for example, sharing or delivering results), with the wording allowing either one or both of them: Model the optional follow-up actions as tasks in the lane or pool of the participant who performs them, sequenced after the end of the automated work. Place an inclusive gateway before the follow-up tasks so that one or both can be chosen. Join the branches again with an inclusive gateway before the end event of that participant, and do not force every follow-up to run.
rules.situation: the description states that after an automated process has finished, a participant may perform one or more optional follow-up actions (for example, sharing or delivering results), with the wording allowing either one or both of them

rules.instruction: When the description says an external occurrence, such as a disruption or a request to change a planned list, can happen at any time during an ongoing activity, and the activity then goes on afterwards: Model the handling of that occurrence as a task whose outgoing sequence flow leads back into the ongoing activity at the step where it was interrupted, so the activity is resumed. Do not end the process or redirect the flow to an unrelated element after the handling task. Do not model the occurrence as a wait unless the description explicitly says the process waits for it.
rules.situation: the description says an external occurrence, such as a disruption or a request to change a planned list, can happen at any time during an ongoing activity, and the activity then goes on afterwards

rules.instruction: When the description names an occurrence that starts the process or decides a gateway, such as a desire to create something, a state the description says is finished, or a notification it says is triggered, and the modeler would otherwise label that start event or gateway question with a paraphrase, abbreviation, or a different occurrence from elsewhere in the description: Label the start event with the description's own term for the desire or goal that starts the process. Label each decision gateway with a question that reuses the exact state or occurrence term the description gives for that decision, and spell out any term the description gives only as an abbreviation or paraphrase. Do not substitute a different occurrence that the description mentions elsewhere, and do not invent a summary label.
rules.situation: the description names an occurrence that starts the process or decides a gateway, such as a desire to create something, a state the description says is finished, or a notification it says is triggered, and the modeler would otherwise label that start event or gateway question with a paraphrase, abbreviation, or a different occurrence from elsewhere in the description

rules.instruction: When the description says that some items are required in order to create other items, so that the creation of an item must happen before another item can be obtained: Model the creation of each prerequisite item as its own task performed by the responsible participant, placed in that participant's lane and before the dependent activity in the sequence. Do not replace the creation with a business rule task that only evaluates dependency rules, and do not drop the creation step.
rules.situation: the description says that some items are required in order to create other items, so that the creation of an item must happen before another item can be obtained
